To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Salmonella was found in beef cattle feedlot feces, feed, soil, and water samples and that phages can be isolated from Salmonella free environments.

Salmonella enterica was isolated from 18.5% (20/108) of samples collected from three beef feedlots in South Texas; Salmonella phages were found in 50% of samples (54/108) collected and were most frequently recovered from soil and fecal samples; and Salmonella phages recovered from Salmonella negative feedlots suggest a potential role for phages in controlling Salmonella populations in the feedlot environment.
Salmonella was found in 18.5% (20/108) of samples collected from feedlot pens, and bacteriophages were found in 44.5% (48/108) of those samples.

this study has demonstrated that phage positive samples were not correlated with Salmonella positive samples.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of Salmonella in beef cattle feedlots is lower than expected, but phages are present and may be useful for controlling this pathogen.
Salmonella was isolated from 18% of samples collected from three feedlots in south texas, with the majority of isolates being S. enterica serovar Anatum.
Salmonella and Salmonellaphages are prevalent in the beef cattle feedlot environment and may play an important role in the ecology of Salmonella in the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Salmonella and phage can be recovered from beef cattle feedlots in south texas and that phages are more prevalent in the feedlot environment than Salmonella.
phage prevalence was not strongly correlated with culturable Salmonella prevalence, but phages were found more often in samples that contained culturable Salmonella than in Salmonella free samples.

Salmonella is present in feedlot environments, that Salmonella phages are also present, that phage recovery is independent of the presence of culturables, and that Salmonella phage prevalence is correlated with sample source.
